question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 64 cm. The length of the rectangle is 3 times of its breadth. What is the length (in cm) of its diagonal?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Length : Breadth = 3 : 1.

Perimeter units = 2 × (3 + 1) = 8 units.

8 units = 64 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 8 cm.

Sides are 24 cm (Length) and 8 cm (Breadth).

Diagonal = 8 × √(3² + 1²) = 8√10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8√10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of rectangle = 64 cm

Length (L) = 3 × Breadth (B)

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2 × (L + B)

Diagonal = √(L² + B²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a31aa2d879a487ae9d6f53a7ef91c4f5886d32d9df6afbc211d52267467dd614.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Breadth be x cm. Then Length = 3x cm.

⇒ 2 × (3x + x) = 64

⇒ 2 × 4x = 64

⇒ 8x = 64 ⇒ x = 8

⇒ Breadth = 8 cm and Length = 3 × 8 = 24 cm.

⇒ Diagonal = √(24² + 8²)

⇒ Diagonal = √(576 + 64)

⇒ Diagonal = √640

⇒ Diagonal = √(64 × 10) = 8√10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8√10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is calculated as Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal Property

The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length and bisect each other at the point of intersection.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle formed by the sides and diagonal, Diagonal² = Length² + Breadth².
